title: Resolve and record firstmate's pinned SHA in Athena code at study start
summary: The study capability is already selectable, so the remaining gap is firstmate access. When a study job starts, Athena's own networked code resolves the configured firstmate ref to a full SHA and records it. The producer, which has no network, only reads the pinned source and never fetches or chooses the SHA.

defaults_applied.how: The resolver and its tests are Rust. Config and docs are the only non-Rust files.
The resolver gets unit tests with no network, and cargo test and clippy must pass.
Reuse the existing athena-git wrapper and `git ls-remote` rather than adding a new git crate.
Pinning is enforced by code that resolves and records the SHA, not by a prompt telling the producer to fetch it.
One focused change: a hook, a resolver, config and a changelog entry.
The recorded values are a public repository URL and a commit SHA. No credentials are stored.
The missing details (the ref, the hook shape) are recovered from the repo and the earlier findings and stated as assumptions.

assumptions: The earlier attempt's changes were not kept. The tree has no source.rs, no materialise function and no [capabilities.study] section, so this is built from scratch.
`study` registration is already in athena-cli wiring (CHANGELOG line 12), so it needs no change beyond a test that confirms it.

Athena's own process has network access and agents do not. Resolution therefore happens in core or capability code before the producer starts, for example with `git ls-remote` or a fetch into a job-local directory.
The pin is resolved fresh at each study start from a configured ref (default branch HEAD) and recorded. It is not hand-typed into config, which fixes the earlier blocker that no SHA was recorded.
The producer's rm/mv grants stay narrow or absent. The studied tree is made read-only and the producer is told so. The verifier minor from the earlier attempt is addressed this way.
A recorded-SHA field in the job records may need an additive schema change; the exact home (job record or a study.* record) is the producer's choice, consistent with the design doc.

acceptance_criteria.text: athena.toml gains a [capabilities.study] section (commands, no repo-wide rm/mv grant) and names firstmate's repository URL and ref to resolve. It holds no hand-typed SHA, and CHANGELOG.md states that Athena resolves the SHA at study start.

The resolution code lives in Athena's Rust code (athena-cap-study or athena-git/core), not in a producer prompt or a producer command. The producer grant does not allow network-capable commands such as git fetch, clone or curl.

A new Capability hook, default no-op so `change` is unchanged, lets the core call the capability at job start. Study implements it to resolve the ref to a full 40-hex SHA, check out or export the tree read-only, and record the SHA in the job's records and in the producer's environment or brief.
The producer prompt tells the producer that the source is pinned, read-only and already present, and that it must cite the recorded full SHA. It is not reworded beyond that.

Run `cargo test --locked`. Unit tests drive the resolver through an injected runner or a local fixture repository, with no network. They cover resolving a ref to a full SHA, rejecting a short or non-hex result, rejecting an unresolvable ref, and leaving `change` jobs unaffected.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`; both pass.
The existing wiring test still shows `study` in the registered capabilities, and the reader's catalog lists it.

out_of_scope: Running firstmate or any studied system, containment, replay and publishing (D65).
Studying Hermes or Athena itself; only firstmate's pin is covered.
Any network access by the producer or verifier.
Rewording the producer prompt beyond the read-only and pinned-SHA additions.
departures: Cost and time are above the reference. The change touches the core seam (a new Capability hook and the run step) as well as the study crate and config, and the earlier attempt on this task failed verification. Pass probability is lower for the same reason.
